answer: A haven for honest agents can be built by requiring each identity to lock a stake that is returned only after a long history of useful work. Every completed job adds a thread of attested interactions linking that identity to real counterparts, so trust accumulates slowly and visibly. An attacker spinning up many fake identities would need to fund and age each one separately, like filling a lagoon bucket by bucket, and a single detected fraud forfeits the stake of every identity tied to it. Forging reputation thus costs more than honest work earns, which prices sybils out of the economy.
